main_text.l: Articulus III.
DE PTOLEMÆO AULETA.
Anni sunt 29. ad annum 3899.
Ptolemæi Auletæ, ab indecoro fistularum
fice dio ficdicti, historia ad tria capita, nimirum
Regimen, antequam ejiceretur, Exilium, & Redi-
tum reduci poteft. Regimen vile admodum erat.
Nam quia amicitiam R. P. totus amplexus
nec hanc, nisi per munera obtinere potuit, Iabal-
tos affligere, ut Cæsari VIM Talentorum, hocceft
quinquagefies quater aureorum centena millia
offerret , necesse habuit. Quin in societatem
receptus, Cyprum Ptolemæo alteri, ex lege à Cato.
Appian. l. 2. dio lata, quod ipsum à piratis captum redimere
noluisset, feripi, &c, eo quæsita morte fabulosa
in provinciæ formam redigi passus est. In exilium
à populo, qui hortulanum aradice oliva rel
findentem odit, pulsus Romam se contulit, & Strabo
l. 17. quidem restitutionem, partim interfectis, partim
corruptis, qui accusatum ex Ægypto venerant,
egatis, impetravit, sed cum interim Sibyllinum
Carmen inventum, militem in Ægyptum
prohiberet, (nulla re multitudo magna regitur
quam superstitione, Puntio temporis mutua
mentarum vertuntur) post aliquantulam ... Ephesum
abiit; Be-renice maxima natu filia, quæ sola legitima erat,
illis aduc infantibus exclusis, regnum invenit,
administratorem. Reditum tandem est a Gabinio,
exercitum contra Parthos educturo, Pompeji
iussu; & redux, victis Alexandrinis, Berenicen
Eliam.
Dio. l. 39.

page.notes: Printed page is a scan with heavy show-through and faint marginal stains; the left margin notes are mostly indistinct. Several words in the body are illegible and marked only roughly; the scan is badly damaged at lines containing Ptolemaeus, Gabinius and Berenice, and the passage near "post aliquantulam" is not reliably readable. The right-hand margin contains only faint fragments and was not transcribed.
